problems.title: Prerequisite operator Job Set Operator is not installed
problems.description: "JobSet Operator" is not installed. It is package job-set in the redhat-operators catalog. It keeps the DataScienceCluster from being Ready.
evidence: DataScienceCluster default-dsc: TrainerReady=False (Error): dependency not met: JobSet Operator is not installed. Please install the JobSet Operator via OLM (OperatorHub) before deploying Trainer.
Catalog: package job-set in catalog redhat-operators (provider Red Hat, Inc.), default channel stable-v1.0, head jobset-operator.v1.0.1
Install modes supported by jobset-operator.v1.0.1: OwnNamespace, SingleNamespace; suggested namespace: openshift-jobset-operator
problems.fix: Install Job Set Operator with the commands below (as a cluster administrator; the tool does not install operators). It goes into its suggested namespace openshift-jobset-operator, watching only that namespace (install mode OwnNamespace, which the CSV supports). The Subscription follows the default channel stable-v1.0 of redhat-operators with automatic updates; the two oc wait lines return once the operator is installed. The last command creates JobSetOperator/cluster from the CSV's example, which the operator needs before it does anything; some operators create it themselves, so it is created only if it is still missing.
problems.technicalCmd:
oc apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: openshift-jobset-operator
  labels:
    openshift.io/cluster-monitoring: "true"
---
apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1
kind: OperatorGroup
metadata:
  name: openshift-jobset-operator
  namespace: openshift-jobset-operator
spec:
  targetNamespaces:
  - openshift-jobset-operator
---
apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1
kind: Subscription
metadata:
  name: job-set
  namespace: openshift-jobset-operator
spec:
  channel: stable-v1.0
  name: job-set
  source: redhat-operators
  sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace
  installPlanApproval: Automatic
EOF
oc wait subscription/job-set -n openshift-jobset-operator '--for=jsonpath={.status.state}=AtLatestKnown' --timeout=10m
oc wait csv/"$(oc get subscription/job-set -n openshift-jobset-operator -o jsonpath='{.status.installedCSV}')" -n openshift-jobset-operator --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded --timeout=10m
oc get jobsetoperator.operator.openshift.io/cluster >/dev/null 2>&1 || oc create -f - <<'EOF'
{
  "apiVersion": "operator.openshift.io/v1",
  "kind": "JobSetOperator",
  "metadata": {
    "name": "cluster"
  },
  "spec": {
    "logLevel": "Normal",
    "managementState": "Managed",
    "operatorLogLevel": "Normal"
  }
}
EOF
